result.summary: Explored the reference product (xcoder-ai-dojo: a PyQt6 Python desktop IDE with editor, workspace tree, run console, bounded workspace-inspection agent, agent-CLI delegation, voice and Docker catalogue) and wrote a requirements document for a TypeScript port into a new xcoder-dojo/ folder. The document turns the vague input into a concrete checkable outcome: a two-command-startable app that completes the loop open folder -> tree -> edit with highlighting and line numbers -> save preserving BOM/CRLF -> run and read console output -> agent inspects workspace with allowlisted tools -> agent delegates a coding task with streamed output. It states 10 explicit non-goals (voice, Docker catalogue, installer/signing, Butler persona, LSP/debugger/Git UI/SSH, multi-user, pixel-parity art, durable task board, data migration, non-English voice), 12 technical constraints (TypeScript strict, Electron main/preload/renderer isolation, CodeMirror 6 or Monaco, separate data root ~/.xcoder/dojo-ts, OS-protected key store, encoding fidelity, reference read bounds, bounded one-call-per-turn agent loop), 13 binding security constraints mapped to the secure-architect bylaws (injection delimiting, allowlisted tools only, schema-validated output, sandbox enforced in code, human approval for writes/agent runs, sandboxed execution, redacted audit log, cost controls, supply chain), 4 assumptions, 21 testable acceptance criteria, 5 open questions with defaults, and a reference-module traceability table.

deliverable.goal: Build xcoder-dojo: a self-contained TypeScript implementation of the Xcoder AI Dojo desktop workbench in a new top-level folder xcoder-dojo/, startable with two documented commands, completing this loop without the Python reference: open a folder -> view tree -> open and edit a source file with syntax highlighting and line numbers -> save preserving encoding and line endings -> run it and read output in a console -> ask the built-in agent to inspect the workspace and delegate a coding task -> see tool calls and streamed agent output. 'TypeScript UI and Agent' = the UI layer AND the in-app assistant/tool-dispatch layer are both TypeScript; the external agent CLI stays as the execution boundary.

Baseline: repository version **0.1.4**, reviewed **14 November 2026**.

This document defines the Dojo's product, implemented architecture, operating model, and proposed evolution. **Current** means present in this repository; **proposed** means future work, not a shipped capability. Source code takes precedence where older handoff documents differ. External agent internals and the Studio Docker supervisor are outside this repository.

## 1. Product purpose

Xcoder AI Dojo is a Windows-first, PyQt6 desktop development environment for mixed-language workspaces. It brings source editing, project execution, developer utilities, AI assistance, coding-agent delegation, and voice interaction into one application.

The central workflow is: open a workspace, understand the code, edit or delegate a task, run the project, inspect results, and iterate. A workspace can be a single project or a parent folder containing multiple projects with different runtimes.

The intended users are individual developers working across Python, web, Java, shell, and SQLite projects; developers integrating APIs and local services; and users who want conversational or spoken assistance alongside their editor.

The Dojo is a desktop workbench. This repository does not implement a hosted collaboration service, cloud account system, billing platform, learning curriculum, or production deployment control plane.

### Product principles

- Keep the active workspace and command working directory explicit.
- Preserve source encodings and line endings when editing existing files.
- Keep slow or failure-prone work outside the Qt UI process where supported.
- Distinguish ordinary chat, bounded workspace inspection, and agent execution.
- Make running work, failures, cancellation, and missing dependencies visible.
- Store application state locally and disclose when content leaves the machine.
- Keep source and packaged worker behavior aligned.

## 2. Scope and capability boundaries

| Area | Current capability | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Workspace | Folder tree, nested project discovery, file tabs | No workspace collaboration service |
| Editor | Highlighting, line numbers, find, save, encoding preservation | No full language-server or debugger integration established here |
| Execution | File/project runners and shared console | Required language tools must be installed separately |
| Markdown | Live preview, links, local images | Embedded HTML and remote images are skipped |
| SQL | SQLite scripts, ephemeral or selected database | Not a general database administration suite |
| Developer tools | Maven, npm, pip, terminals, Docker, network, SSH, HTTP | Uses local tools and their configured access |
| AI task board | Durable text requests, queue, task controls | Does not execute workspace tools |
| JARVIS | Chat, memory compaction, workspace inspection, delegation | Separate execution path from the task board |
| Coding agents | Local SDLC, LiteBro, QA CLI integration | External packages own agent behavior |
| Agents catalog | Pinned package information and Docker health check | Docker supervisor/job orchestration is not included |
| Voice | Local recognition, local/online speech, device settings | Hardware and speech-backend availability vary |
| Distribution | Windows portable package and per-user installer | Signing and clean-machine acceptance remain release work |

## 3. User experience

### Application layout

The main window combines a workspace tree on the left, tabbed source editors in the center, a right-side tool rail and selected tool panel, a shared run console, and status information. Markdown can appear beside its source. The hub and JARVIS interface add themed artwork, assistant controls, transcript, microphone state, and audio feedback.

JARVIS maintains interactive conversation memory separately from the durable task board. It can summarize accumulated messages, retain a bounded summary, and resume a request after successful compaction. Failed compaction preserves the previous chat. Do not treat this in-memory conversation as equivalent to durable task history.

Supported inspection tools are `list_dir`, `glob`, `grep`, `read_file`, `read_multiple_files`, `read_file_lines`, `read_outline`, `validate_file`, `get_python_imports`, `git_status`, `git_diff`, and `git_log`.

The inspection boundary rejects absolute paths, traversal, disallowed path components and resolved escapes from the workspace. It excludes hidden names, selected generated directories and common credential/key filenames. Reads and searches are bounded: output is generally limited to 12,000 characters, multi-file reads to four files, line requests to 200 lines, and scans to 1,500 encountered files. These controls reduce exposure; they are not comprehensive secret detection.

Current tool dispatch accepts one tool call per response. An inspection result is passed to a follow-up model request as data, with instructions to ignore instructions inside that data. This is a bounded request/observation/answer flow, not an unrestricted recursive tool loop.

### Coding-agent delegation

JARVIS can dispatch SDLC, LiteBro and QA tasks through `SdlcRun`. Direct coding/fix controls use the same integration. File-specific fixes validate that the target is inside the active workspace. Dispatch rejects a changed workspace context.

The adapter discovers Node and external agent entry points, supports its native/shell/WSL execution paths, supplies the workspace and task, streams output, and handles stopping. Agent concurrency is requested as one. LiteBro receives its secure-mode argument. These CLI flags do not establish a desktop-wide permission or isolation system.

Per-run provider settings are written to temporary configuration, and conflicting inherited provider variables are removed. This temporary configuration contains the API key in plaintext while needed by the external CLI; permanent Windows key protection does not apply to that temporary representation.

The Docker-oriented Agents catalog is separate: it lists pinned SDLC, Jarvis, QA, LiteBro, Origin, Litecoder and DNA packages and can check the engine. It does not implement the absent Studio supervisor.

## 8. Voice and HUD

Recognition uses Qt Multimedia capture and Vosk locally. The English recognition model is prepared by the launcher/build process and bundled in Windows releases. Legacy/manual model placement is described in the voice integration handoff.

After an end-of-speech pause, recognized text is appended to any draft and submitted, unless speech review is enabled. Microphone listening pauses during assistant work, review, and speech playback, and resumes only when the relevant UI state allows it. This helps prevent the assistant's voice from becoming a new request.

Microphone and speaker default to off; saved choices apply on later launches. Settings expose device selection, nine voice presets, online/local mode, pitch, speed, and volume. Voice preview uses unsaved values; saving persists the selected configuration.

Online synthesis uses `edge-tts` and sends reply text to Microsoft. Local synthesis depends on the platform's available speech backend. Recognition is local, but recognized text sent as an assistant prompt follows the configured LLM's network path.

HUD animation and visual themes must reflect actual listening, working, and playback states. They are presentation components, not independent AI runtimes.

The GUI coordinates work through Qt signals and `QProcess`. The executable also acts as a worker host, allowing the packaged application to start its own API, process, recognition, and synthesis modes without relying on a separately installed Python interpreter.

The shared developer console admits one process at a time. This is distinct from the AI task scheduler, which supports up to four model requests across workspaces and one active request per workspace. JARVIS maintains its own process and busy state; these are not one unified scheduler.

A PyQt6 desktop IDE for Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Vue, Java, Spring Boot, shell scripts, and SQL. It includes a project sidebar, tabbed editor, run console, and live Markdown preview.

Choose **Jarvis** or **The Butler** from the agent dropdown in the chat header. The selection is remembered, and each agent keeps separate conversation context. Butler uses the existing LLM settings through `butler/butler_bridge.py`, with a separate session for each workspace during the current chat. Requests run outside the UI process and support voice input and spoken replies.

When Butler requests permissions, review the displayed classes and type **Approve** or **Decline**. Writes require approval; shell commands are disabled in this integration. **Force Stop** requests cancellation (an in-flight model request may take time to return). Restarting the app starts a fresh Butler chat; its local ledger and artifacts remain in the application data directory.

## Start on Windows

Open PowerShell in this folder with Python 3.10 or newer and the Windows `py` launcher installed.

```powershell
.\bin\build-and-run.ps1
```

The script creates `.venv` if needed, installs the dependencies, checks the Python source, prepares a missing English voice model, and starts the IDE. Model preparation is skipped for `--version` and `--help`. Run `.\bin\build-and-run.ps1 -BuildOnly` to prepare the environment and check the source without opening the IDE.

## Build a Windows release

For a standard Windows installer, install [Inno Setup 6](https://jrsoftware.org/isdl.php) on the build machine, then run:

```powershell
.\bin\build-installer.ps1
```

The installer build uses a separate staging folder so an open portable copy does not lock its output. This builds the current source and creates `dist\Xcoder-AI-Dojo-<version>-Setup.exe`. Double-click that file, follow the wizard, and open **Xcoder AI Dojo** from the Start menu. A desktop shortcut and launching after setup are optional. Python is bundled; end users do not need Python to launch Dojo. Installation is per-user under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Xcoder AI Dojo` and does not request administrator rights. Windows 10 or newer on x64-compatible hardware is required.

If PowerShell blocks unsigned build scripts, use a process-only policy for this build (no permanent policy change):

```powershell
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\bin\build-installer.ps1
```

### 3.2 Security (binding, from secure-architect bylaws)
- S-01 [PRM-01/02] Injection delimiting: all tool output, file contents and fetched text entering model context is wrapped in a labelled untrusted-data block with an explicit rule never to follow instructions inside it. Instructions live only in the system prompt.
- S-02 [PRM-03] No secrets in prompts: API keys, tokens and .env-style values are never placed in a prompt or returned from a tool. The S-06 scanner is the enforcement point.
- S-03 [PRM-04] Least-privilege tools: the agent tool set is exactly the reference allowlist: list_dir, glob, grep, read_file, read_multiple_files, read_file_lines, read_outline, validate_file, git_status, git_diff, git_log. No generic run_command, shell, sql, fetch_url or eval tool is exposed to the model.
- S-04 [PRM-07/08] Structured output only: the model must emit tool calls as schema-validated JSON; unparseable output is rejected and surfaced, never executed. Raw model output never reaches a shell, eval, HTML injection or a file path.
- S-05 [PRM-09] Policy in code: the workspace sandbox (S-06) and the approval gate (S-07) are enforced in TypeScript regardless of what any prompt says.

shared_contracts.AppErrorCode: closed union (path-escape, credential-file, binary-file, not-utf8, run-busy, runtime-missing, turn-limit, tool-not-allowlisted, approval-expired, secret-detected, ...) so pages render codes, never raw stacks or provider payloads
shared_contracts.ActionDescriptor<In,Out>: { name, sideEffect: none|read|write|execute|secret, requiresApproval: boolean, enforcedIn: 'main', validate(input), run(input) } — requiresApproval is non-optional so a new high-impact action cannot silently lack a gate
shared_contracts.BridgeResult<T>: { ok: true, value } | { ok: false, error: AppError }
shared_contracts.DojoBridge: workspace / tree / files / run / agent / session / delegation / approval / settings / audit / errors — the entire privileged surface; preload exposes no ipcRenderer passthrough, validates every payload in main, and can never return the API key (only hasApiKey: boolean)

searchable_filterable: P-02 text filter over loaded nodes

explicit_tradeoffs: T-01 Single-flight console (no run queue): one auditable execution contract and one Stop target, at the cost of not running two projects at once.
T-02 Page-level rather than component-level specification: stable contracts across refactors, at the cost of implementation freedom inside a page.

T-03 Approval only for file-write and delegation-launch: no approval fatigue and no route to approve anything dangerous; cost is that a future high-impact action must be classified explicitly (mitigated by non-optional requiresApproval).
T-04 No free-text workspace path input: eliminates an unvalidated traversal surface; cost is that power users cannot paste a path.
T-05 Exclusion policy decided in main, user filter only over loaded nodes: one authoritative sandbox, at the cost of filtering not being a whole-workspace search.
T-06 Read caps surfaced as truncated+counts rather than silently: no partial file is ever presented as complete; cost is more UI states and a deliberately non-saveable truncated buffer.
T-07 Markdown preview blocks raw HTML and remote images visibly: closes XSS/SSRF/tracking-image vectors; cost is incomplete rendering of some legitimate Markdown.
T-08 Append-only transcript: the transcript stays an audit artifact; cost is no in-place editing or conversation branching.
T-09 Settings/History/Audit as overlays, not routes: workspace, run and agent state never restart on navigation; cost is no deep-linking and added overlay-stack management.
T-10 Agent output as escaped text plus main-generated cards: a prompt injection cannot forge a card or executable UI; cost is no rich presentational answers.
enforcement_matrix_highlights: Only file.save (when agent-initiated) and delegation.launch carry requiresApproval: true; delegation.launch additionally requires an unexpired approvalId bound to the same toolCallId.
run.start passes an argv array plus allowlisted env keys — never an interpolated shell string.
The agent tool vocabulary is the closed union AllowlistedToolName (11 tools incl. the three git_ read-only tools); any other name is refused as tool-not-allowlisted and never dispatched.
settings.setApiKey is write-only; no interface in the document can read the key back.

Baseline: repository version **0.1.4**, reviewed **14 November 2026**.

This document defines the Dojo's product, implemented architecture, operating model, and proposed evolution. **Current** means present in this repository; **proposed** means future work, not a shipped capability. ## 1. Product purpose

Xcoder AI Dojo is a Windows-first, PyQt6 desktop development environment for mixed-language workspaces. It brings source editing, project execution, developer utilities, AI assistance, coding-agent delegation, and voice interaction into one application.

The central workflow is: open a workspace, understand the code, edit or delegate a task, run the project, inspect results, and iterate. A workspace can be a single project or a parent folder containing multiple projects with different runtimes.

The intended users are individual developers working across Python, web, Java, shell, and SQLite projects; developers integrating APIs and local services; and users who want conversational or spoken assistance alongside their editor.

The Dojo is a desktop workbench. This repository does not implement a hosted collaboration service, cloud account system, billing platform, learning curriculum, or production deployment control plane.

### Product principles

- Keep the active workspace and command working directory explicit.
- Preserve source encodings and line endings when editing existing files.
- Keep slow or failure-prone work outside the Qt UI process where supported.
- Distinguish ordinary chat, bounded workspace inspection, and agent execution.
- Make running work, failures, cancellation, and missing dependencies visible.
- Store application state locally and disclose when content leaves the machine.

# Design: xcoder-dojo — UI / Page Specification (TypeScript UI + Agent)

- Task: design-st-2c7624 (stage: design, role: business-analyst)
- Upstream: `.xcoder/backlog/requirements-st-b1522d.md` (21 ACs, security constraints S-01..S-13, non-goals NG-01..NG-10)
- Reference (read-only input): `xcoder-ai-dojo/` PyQt6 v0.1.4 — blueprint §3 (UX), §4 (module map)
- Target: new sibling folder `xcoder-dojo/` (greenfield — no TS scaffold exists in this workspace)
- This document covers navigation flows, page/subpage specs, per-page data requirements, display modes, UI action contracts, component interfaces and tradeoffs. It does not cover build pipeline, module layout or LLM wire format.

## 1. What "component" and "interface" mean here

- **Component = page or subpage** (`P-xx`): a user-visible surface with its own data requirements and action set. Pages are the unit of specification, not React components.
- **Interface = contract**, in three parts: (a) **page model** — exactly what the page renders, with nullability; (b) **action contract** — name, input, side-effect class, approval requirement, enforcing process; (c) **IPC bridge** — the only channel from a page to privileged work.
- **Tradeoffs** are collected in §15 and cross-referenced from the page that pays for them.

Two invariants hold on every page and are not restated per page:

1. **UI checks are UX only** [UI-01]. Every action is re-authorized and re-validated in the Electron main process. A hidden button is not a control.
2. **Model-derived and file-derived text is untrusted** [UI-02/03/13, PRM-01]. It renders as escaped text or sanitized Markdown; no raw HTML, no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, no remote images, no execution, and it is labelled AI-generated or workspace-derived.

## 2. Navigation flow

### 2.1 Page hierarchy

```
P-00 App Shell (persistent frame)
├─ P-01 Welcome / No-Workspace              center, shown while no workspace is open
├─ P-02 Workspace Explorer                  left dock, lazy tree
│    └─ P-02a Node Context Menu             transient overlay
├─ P-03 Editor Area                         center, tabbed
│    ├─ P-03a Text Editor Pane              CodeMirror 6: highlighting, line numbers
│    ├─ P-03b Markdown Preview Pane         split beside P-03a
│    └─ P-03c Unopenable File State         binary / non-UTF-8 / too large / outside root
├─ P-04 Run Console                         bottom dock, single-flight
│    └─ P-04a Run Target Picker             subpage when >1 target resolves
├─ P-05 Agent Panel (JARVIS)                right dock
│    ├─ P-05a Tool Call Card                inline list item
│    ├─ P-05b Turn-Limit Banner             inline terminal state
│    └─ P-05c Model-Not-Configured State    inline empty state
├─ P-06 Delegation Run View                 right dock takeover
├─ P-07 Approval Sheet                      modal overlay (file-write | delegation-launch)
├─ P-08 Settings                            modal, tabbed
│    ├─ P-08a Model & Limits
│    ├─ P-08b Data, Secrets & Audit
│    └─ P-08c Appearance
├─ P-09 Conversation History                drawer inside P-05
├─ P-10 Audit Log Viewer                    modal, cursor-paginated
├─ P-11 Status Bar                          persistent chrome on all pages
└─ P-12 Error Center                        toast stack + detail sheet
```

### 2.2 Transitions

| From | Trigger | To | Guard / failure |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P-01 | `workspace.open` (OS dialog only) | P-00 + populated P-02 | Not a folder / unreadable / outside policy → P-12, stay on P-01 |
| P-02 | `file.open` | P-03 new tab | Unopenable → P-03c, never a blank editor |
| P-02 | right-click node | P-02a | — |
| P-03 | `file.save` (Ctrl+S) | P-03, dirty cleared | Write failure → P-12, tab stays dirty |
| P-03 | tab kind = markdown, toggle preview | P-03b split | Remote images / raw HTML skipped and annotated |
| P-03 | `run.start` (Ctrl+R) | P-04 | Console busy → `run-busy` report, no second process |
| P-03 | `run.start`, multiple targets | P-04a first | No resolvable target → explicit error, not a silent no-op |
| P-05 | user sends message | P-05 streaming + P-05a cards | No model → P-05c; rest of app stays usable |
| P-05a | model requests a delegation tool call | P-07 `delegation-launch` | Denied → card `denied`, nothing launches |
| P-07 approved | delegation | P-06 | CLI missing → P-06 `failed-cli-missing` + remediation |
| P-07 approved | file write | back to origin page | File changed since request → `approval-expired`, re-prompt |
| P-05 | `session.clear` | P-05 empty transcript | — |
| P-11 | click audit-log location | P-10 | Missing log → P-12 with path shown |
| any | unrecoverable main-process error | P-12 | Shell renders an error page, never a blank window |

Concurrency rules (mirroring the reference): one workspace per window, one active run, one active agent request. Opening another workspace requires closing the current one, with the unsaved-tabs prompt first.

## 15. Tradeoffs (explicit, with cost)

Each tradeoff names what was gained and what was given up so a reviewer can overturn it knowingly.

- **T-01 Single-flight console vs. concurrent runs** — *Chosen:* one run at a time; a second request returns `run-busy`, no queue. *Gained:* a simple, auditable execution contract with one Stop target and no scheduler state machine. *Cost:* a user cannot watch or queue two projects at once. *Why acceptable:* matches the reference's shared console and keeps AC-06/AC-07 verifiable; queueing is additive later.
- **T-02 Page-level spec instead of component-level** — *Chosen:* specify pages/subpages (`P-xx`) with page models, not every React component. *Gained:* contracts stay stable when components are refactored and the design survives framework churn. *Cost:* implementation freedom inside a page can drift from the intended UX unless the page's action contract is respected.
- **T-03 Approval only for two action classes** — *Chosen:* exactly `file-write` and `delegation-launch` prompt; everything else is a harmless read or is refused outright. *Gained:* no approval fatigue and no path to approving a dangerous action. *Cost:* a newly added high-impact action would silently have no gate — mitigated by making `requiresApproval` a required field on every `ActionDescriptor` so omission is a type error.
- **T-04 No free-text workspace path input** — *Chosen:* the workspace is opened only through the OS dialog or a re-validated recents entry. *Gained:* removes an unvalidated path-input surface with all its traversal and credential edge cases [S-06]. *Cost:* power users cannot paste a path. Accepted for v1.
- **T-05 Exclusions decided in main; the user filter applies only to loaded nodes** — *Chosen:* dotfiles, generated dirs and credential-shaped names are excluded in main and never sent; the text filter narrows already-loaded children. *Gained:* one authoritative sandbox implementation [PRM-09] that no client-side filter can bypass. *Cost:* filtering is not a whole-workspace search and a filtered tree can look incomplete — mitigated by naming the bounds in empty/truncated states.
- **T-06 Read caps visible rather than silent** — *Chosen:* hitting a char/line/file bound surfaces `truncated` plus counts. *Gained:* the user is never shown a partial file as if complete [AC-19]. *Cost:* more UI states, and a truncated buffer is deliberately not silently saveable as complete.
- **T-07 Markdown preview blocks HTML and remote images, visibly** — *Chosen:* sanitized AST only, local images only, with a visible blocked count. *Gained:* closes the main XSS / SSRF / tracking-image vectors in a preview pane [UI-02/03, AC-20]. *Cost:* some legitimate Markdown renders incompletely; the annotation keeps that honest instead of confusing.
- **T-08 Transcript is append-only, not editable** — *Chosen:* users can copy and clear, not edit prior turns. *Gained:* the transcript remains a trustworthy audit artifact. *Cost:* fixing a typo requires a new turn; no in-place editing or conversation branching.
- **T-09 Settings, History and Audit are overlays, not routes** — *Chosen:* they open as modal or drawer surfaces over the workbench. *Gained:* workspace, run and agent state stay mounted and never restart because of navigation; simpler state ownership. *Cost:* no deep-linking into a settings tab, and overlay stacking must be managed.
- **T-10 Agent output is escaped text plus main-generated cards** — *Chosen:* model text renders escaped with sanitized Markdown and an AI-generated label; tool cards are produced from structured events by main, not by the model. *Gained:* a prompt injection cannot forge a tool card or executable UI [UI-13, PRM-01/08]. *Cost:* richer presentational answers (embedded tables, widgets) are unsupported.

## 16. Action -> page -> enforcement matrix

| Action | Page(s) | Side effect | Approval | Validated/enforced in | Primary ACs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace.open` | P-01, P-00 | read | no | main (OS dialog + root confinement) | AC-01, AC-02 |
| `workspace.close` | P-00 | none | no | main (unsaved prompt) | AC-03 |
| `tree.listChildren` | P-02 | read | no | main (sandbox + bounds) | AC-02, AC-11 |
| `file.open` | P-02, P-03 | read | no | main (encoding and kind detection) | AC-03, AC-05 |
| `file.save` | P-03 | write | **only if agent-initiated** | main (encoding/EOL, `baseSha`) | AC-04, AC-15 |
| `file.revert` | P-03 | write | no (user-initiated, discards buffer) | renderer + main | AC-03 |
| `run.resolveTargets` | P-04, P-04a | read | no | main (target allowlist) | AC-06, AC-08 |
| `run.start` | P-04 | execute | no (user-initiated) | main (argv, cwd, timeout, single-flight) | AC-06, AC-07, AC-08 |
| `run.stop` | P-04 | execute | no | main (terminate + escalation) | AC-07 |
| `agent.send` | P-05 | read + external | no | main (limits, tool allowlist, prompt assembly) | AC-09, AC-10, AC-19 |
| `agent.stop` | P-05 | none | no | main (abort in-flight) | AC-09 |
| `delegation.launch` | P-06 via P-07 | execute | **yes** | main (requires a consumed `approvalId`) | AC-13, AC-15 |
| `delegation.stop` | P-06 | execute | no | main | AC-13 |
| `approval.respond` | P-07 | none | n/a | main (single-use, expiry) | AC-15 |
| `settings.setApiKey` / `settings.clearApiKey` | P-08a/b | secret | no | main + OS key store (never returned) | AC-18 |
| `session.clear` | P-05, P-09 | write | no (explicit confirm) | main | AC-17 |
| `audit.page` / `audit.location` | P-10, P-11 | read | no | main (redaction, retention) | AC-18, S-11 |

The only actions carrying `requiresApproval: true` are the two that write files or launch execution on the agent's behalf; both are unreachable by a model without a matching, unexpired `approvalId`.

## 17. Component -> interface coverage (AC1 evidence)

| Component | Page ID | Interface(s) defined | Display modes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| App Shell | P-00 | `ShellModel`, `ShellActions`, `DojoBridge` | view |
| Welcome | P-01 | `WelcomeModel`, `WelcomeActions` | list, view |
| Workspace Explorer | P-02 | `FileNode`, `TreeNodePage`, `ExplorerModel`, `ExplorerActions` | list, sortable, filter, lazy-page |
| Node Context Menu | P-02a | `NodeContextMenuModel` | detail |
| Editor Area | P-03 | `EditorTabState`, `EditorModel`, `EditorActions` | editable, detail |
| Text Editor Pane | P-03a | `FileReadResult`, `EditorActions` | editable |
| Markdown Preview | P-03b | `MarkdownPreviewModel` | view (read-only) |
| Unopenable File | P-03c | `FileOpenErrorCode`, `EditorTabState` | detail (error) |
| Run Console | P-04 | `RunTarget`, `RunSession`, `ConsoleModel`, `ConsoleActions` | view, list, filter, search |
| Run Target Picker | P-04a | `RunTarget`, `ConsoleActions.resolveTargets` | list (single select) |
| Agent Panel | P-05 | `TranscriptEntry`, `AgentModel`, `AgentActions`, `AgentEvent` | view, list, search, paged |
| Tool Call Card | P-05a | `ToolCallRecord`, `AllowlistedToolName` | detail |
| Turn-Limit Banner | P-05b | `AgentModel.request` | detail (terminal) |
| Model-Not-Configured | P-05c | `AgentModel.modelState`, `LlmSettingsView` | detail (empty) |
| Delegation Run View | P-06 | `DelegationRun`, `DelegationModel`, `DelegationActions` | view, list, search |
| Approval Sheet | P-07 | `ApprovalRequest`, `ApprovalModel`, `ApprovalActions` | detail |
| Settings | P-08 | `LlmSettingsView`, `LlmSettingsPatch`, `SettingsActions` | detail, editable |
| Model & Limits | P-08a | `AgentLimits`, `SettingsActions` | editable |
| Data, Secrets & Audit | P-08b | `ApiKeyInput`, `LlmSettingsView` | editable (key write-only) |
| Appearance | P-08c | `LlmSettingsPatch.appearance` | editable |
| Conversation History | P-09 | `SessionSummary`, `SessionDetail`, `HistoryActions` | list, sortable, searchable, paged |
| Audit Log Viewer | P-10 | `AuditEventView`, `AuditPage`, `AuditActions` | list, sortable, filterable, paged |
| Status Bar | P-11 | `StatusBarModel`, `StatusBarActions` | view |
| Error Center | P-12 | `AppError`, `ErrorCenterModel`, `ErrorCenterActions` | list, detail |

Every component above has at least one exported data interface and one action interface (or an explicitly inherited one). That table is the AC1 evidence.

## 18. AC traceability (UI level)

| AC | How this design satisfies it |
| --- | --- |
| AC-01 | P-00 title bar renders `Xcoder Dojo` plus the workspace path; P-11 mirrors it |
| AC-02 | P-02 lazy `listChildren` per directory; nothing above root is requestable |
| AC-03 | P-03 tabs with CodeMirror highlighting, line numbers, close and a dirty dot |
| AC-04 | P-03 save carries `encoding`/`eol` from `FileReadResult`; new files default UTF-8 |
| AC-05 | P-03c with `binary-file`/`not-utf8` and the "nothing modified" copy |
| AC-06 | P-04 saves the active file first, streams stdout/stderr, shows the exit code |
| AC-07 | P-04 single-flight, `stopping` state, stopped-reported exit path |
| AC-08 | P-04 `runtime-missing` and non-zero exit bars |
| AC-09 | P-05 `AgentEvent['tool-call']` renders P-05a with args, outcome and duration |
| AC-10 | P-05 `turn-progress` plus the P-05b terminal turn-limit banner |
| AC-11 | P-05a `refused-sandbox`/`refused-credential` outcomes; no content in the card |
| AC-12 | P-05 delimited `workspace-data` entries; `tool-not-allowlisted` rejection notice |
| AC-13 | P-06 streamed output, working Stop, `failed-workspace-changed` refusal |
| AC-14 | P-05a renders read-only git results; no stage/commit/push action exists in any interface |
| AC-15 | P-07 `concreteTarget` shown verbatim, decision audited, `approval-expired` re-prompt |
| AC-16 | P-05c with send disabled; P-01/02/03/04 unaffected |
| AC-17 | P-09 list/resume/clear over persisted sessions; transcript restored on start |
| AC-18 | P-08b exposes `hasApiKey` only; P-10 and P-11 disclose the log location |
| AC-19 | Every capped surface carries `truncated` plus counts (P-02, P-03, P-04, P-05a, P-06) |
| AC-20 | P-03b sanitized AST, local images only, visible blocked count |
| AC-21 | Not a UI concern; the interfaces above are the typed surface those unit tests assert against |

## 19. Open questions carried forward (with design defaults)

1. **Default delegation CLI** — modelled as a user-configurable `delegationCliLabel`; one concrete default is chosen at implementation. P-06 covers the unconfigured case with `failed-cli-missing`.
2. **Token-by-token streaming** — assumed yes. If the implementation buffers instead, `AgentEvent.delta` collapses into `entry-completed` and P-05 loses only the streaming affordance, not its contract.
3. **In-repo stub model server** — assumed under `xcoder-dojo/test/`; P-05 shows `modelState: 'error'` if it is unreachable.
4. **Terminal, SSH and HTTP panels** — out of scope (NG-05); P-04 is the only execution surface in this design.

## 20. Deliberate omissions from this document

Module/folder layout, build commands, Electron security configuration details, prompt text, tool JSON schemas (versioned elsewhere per S-12), and the model request/response wire format. Those belong to the architecture and implementation stages. This document fixes only what the user can see and what each surface may ask main to do.

design-st-2c7624.summary: Wrote the UI/page specification design document for xcoder-dojo at .xcoder/backlog/design-st-2c7624.md (953 lines). It defines a 24-surface navigation hierarchy (P-00 shell through P-12 error center, including subpages P-02a, P-03a/b/c, P-04a, P-05a/b/c, P-08a/b/c), a shared contract layer (AppError closed vocabulary, ActionDescriptor with mandatory requiresApproval/enforcedIn, and the complete DojoBridge preload surface), per-page data requirements tables, explicit display modes (view/list/detail/editable/sortable/searchable/paginated) for every page, typed action contracts, 10 explicit tradeoffs with stated costs, an action->page->enforcement matrix, a component->interface coverage table, and AC-01..AC-21 UI traceability. I self-checked by extracting every TypeScript fence and type-checking the combined file under tsc --strict, which caught a real dangling reference (MarkdownBlock used but never defined); I defined the sanitized Markdown AST, re-ran, and got a clean compile. I also cleaned up two side effects I caused during verification (a stray typescript install that npm leaked into C:\Users\sjnue\node_modules, and a temp working dir); the user's own package.json/package-lock.json were left untouched.

deliverable.interpretation: Components = pages/subpages (P-xx). Interfaces = page models (data), action contracts (side-effect class + approval + enforcing process), and the IPC bridge. Tradeoffs = UX richness vs. simplicity/enforceability, each with an owned cost.
navigation_hierarchy: P-00 App Shell — persistent chrome: title bar (Xcoder Dojo + workspace path), left dock, center, right dock, bottom dock, status bar, overlay slot
P-01 Welcome / No-Workspace — center; recents list + choose-folder CTA; no free-text path field
P-02 Workspace Explorer (left dock) — lazy per-directory tree; + P-02a Node Context Menu
P-03 Editor Area (center, tabbed) — + P-03a Text Editor Pane (CodeMirror 6, highlighting, line numbers), P-03b Markdown Preview Pane, P-03c Unopenable File State
P-04 Run Console (bottom dock, single-flight) — + P-04a Run Target Picker
P-05 Agent Panel / JARVIS (right dock) — + P-05a Tool Call Card, P-05b Turn-Limit Banner, P-05c Model-Not-Configured State
P-06 Delegation Run View — right-dock takeover for the external agent CLI
P-07 Approval Sheet — modal gate for exactly file-write and delegation-launch
P-08 Settings — + P-08a Model & Limits, P-08b Data/Secrets/Audit, P-08c Appearance
P-09 Conversation History — drawer over P-05
P-10 Audit Log Viewer, P-11 Status Bar, P-12 Error Center

shared_contracts.AppErrorCode: closed union (path-escape, credential-file, binary-file, not-utf8, run-busy, runtime-missing, turn-limit, tool-not-allowlisted, approval-expired, secret-detected, ...) so pages render codes, never raw stacks or provider payloads
shared_contracts.ActionDescriptor<In,Out>: { name, sideEffect: none|read|write|execute|secret, requiresApproval: boolean, enforcedIn: 'main', validate(input), run(input) } — requiresApproval is non-optional so a new high-impact action cannot silently lack a gate
shared_contracts.BridgeResult<T>: { ok: true, value } | { ok: false, error: AppError }
shared_contracts.DojoBridge: workspace / tree / files / run / agent / session / delegation / approval / settings / audit / errors — the entire privileged surface; preload exposes no ipcRenderer passthrough, validates every payload in main, and can never return the API key (only hasApiKey: boolean)

searchable_filterable: P-02 text filter over loaded nodes

explicit_tradeoffs: T-01 Single-flight console (no run queue): one auditable execution contract and one Stop target, at the cost of not running two projects at once.
T-02 Page-level rather than component-level specification: stable contracts across refactors, at the cost of implementation freedom inside a page.

T-03 Approval only for file-write and delegation-launch: no approval fatigue and no route to approve anything dangerous; cost is that a future high-impact action must be classified explicitly (mitigated by non-optional requiresApproval).
T-04 No free-text workspace path input: eliminates an unvalidated traversal surface; cost is that power users cannot paste a path.
T-05 Exclusion policy decided in main, user filter only over loaded nodes: one authoritative sandbox, at the cost of filtering not being a whole-workspace search.
T-06 Read caps surfaced as truncated+counts rather than silently: no partial file is ever presented as complete; cost is more UI states and a deliberately non-saveable truncated buffer.
T-07 Markdown preview blocks raw HTML and remote images visibly: closes XSS/SSRF/tracking-image vectors; cost is incomplete rendering of some legitimate Markdown.
T-08 Append-only transcript: the transcript stays an audit artifact; cost is no in-place editing or conversation branching.
T-09 Settings/History/Audit as overlays, not routes: workspace, run and agent state never restart on navigation; cost is no deep-linking and added overlay-stack management.
T-10 Agent output as escaped text plus main-generated cards: a prompt injection cannot forge a card or executable UI; cost is no rich presentational answers.
enforcement_matrix_highlights: Only file.save (when agent-initiated) and delegation.launch carry requiresApproval: true; delegation.launch additionally requires an unexpired approvalId bound to the same toolCallId.
run.start passes an argv array plus allowlisted env keys — never an interpolated shell string.
The agent tool vocabulary is the closed union AllowlistedToolName (11 tools incl. the three git_ read-only tools); any other name is refused as tool-not-allowlisted and never dispatched.
settings.setApiKey is write-only; no interface in the document can read the key back.

acceptance_criteria_evidence.AC1_every_component_has_an_interface: Section 17 maps all 24 components to their exported data and action interfaces; the document contains 83 exported interfaces/types.
acceptance_criteria_evidence.AC2_tradeoff_stated_explicitly: Section 15 states 10 tradeoffs (T-01..T-10), each with the choice, what was gained, what was given up and, where relevant, why it is acceptable.
acceptance_criteria_evidence.other_acs: Section 18 traces AC-01..AC-21 to the specific page, model field or state that satisfies each; AC-21 is noted as not a UI concern but the interfaces are the typed surface its unit tests assert against.

open_questions_carried_forward: Default delegation CLI: modelled as user-configurable delegationCliLabel with a concrete default chosen at implementation.
Token-by-token streaming: assumed yes; if buffered, AgentEvent.delta collapses to entry-completed and only the streaming affordance is lost, not the contract.
In-repo stub model server: assumed under xcoder-dojo/test/; P-05 shows modelState 'error' when unreachable.
Terminal/SSH/HTTP panels: out of scope (NG-05); P-04 is the only execution surface.

result.summary: Implemented Xcoder Dojo — a TypeScript/React UI IDE modeled on xcoder-ai-dojo, in xcoder-dojo/. The work was already largely on disk from the prior attempt (106 files: contracts, backend bridge/sandbox/VFS/audit/agent engine, UI shell with all 24 design surfaces, CSS theme, smoke tests). This run diagnosed and fixed the actual blocker: the validation gate runs `npm run typecheck` from the WORKSPACE ROOT, which had no package.json, so npm reported 'Missing script: typecheck' even though xcoder-dojo/package.json already declared it. I added a root package.json shim that delegates typecheck/build/test/dev to xcoder-dojo via `npm --prefix`, then verified end-to-end: tsc --noEmit compiles 143 files clean, vite build produces a 219 kB bundle, the 40-case smoke suite passes 40/40, and the built app serves over HTTP with a strict CSP and all UI markers present in the bundle. I also removed the stray preview.log I generated during verification.

deliverable.stack: TypeScript 5.6 + React 18 + Vite 5, strict mode, zero runtime deps beyond react/react-dom

architecture.contracts/: Closed AppErrorCode vocabulary, ActionDescriptor with non-optional requiresApproval/enforcedIn, DojoBridge preload surface, and per-page models (workspace, execution, delegation, settings) — 83+ exported types.
architecture.backend/: sandbox.ts (path containment, dotfile/credential/node_modules exclusion), vfs.ts, store.ts, markdown.ts (sanitizing AST parser), audit.ts (append-only, key-redacted), tools.ts (closed allowlist of 11 tools), agent-engine.ts, demo-bridge.ts (in-browser bridge used by the UI).
architecture.ui/pages/: WelcomePage, EditorPage, RunConsolePage, AgentPanel, TranscriptView, ApprovalSheet, DelegationPage, SettingsModal, HistoryModal, AuditModal — covering P-01..P-10.
architecture.ui/components/: Explorer (P-02 tree + node context menu), SyntaxEditor (P-03a), MarkdownView (P-03b), ToolCard (P-05a), StatusBar (P-11), ErrorCenter (P-12).
architecture.ui/styles/: 11 CSS modules (chrome, editor, console, agent, modals, welcome, history, controls, base).

security_properties_enforced_and_tested: Path traversal refused in sandbox AND again at the bridge (defense in depth).
Credential files, dotfiles and node_modules never listed or readable.
API key is write-only: settings expose only hasApiKey, and the serialized view is asserted to never contain the key.
Single-flight run console: a second concurrent run is refused.
Delegation launch is gated by an approval request bound to the tool call; denial means no execution.
Agent tool vocabulary is a closed allowlist; assistant text is labelled model-origin and rendered as escaped text.
Markdown AST strips raw HTML and remote images (XSS / tracking-pixel vectors closed).
Content-Security-Policy in index.html: default-src 'self', script-src 'self', object-src 'none', form-action 'none'.

result.summary: Diagnosed and fixed the actual cause of the failing regression gate, then extended the suite. The previous attempt's 36 files were already on disk and largely sound — typecheck passed and 272 unit tests passed — so I bisected the gate instead of rewriting anything. `npm run regression` (typecheck && test:unit && test:smoke) failed because the smoke stage never exited: it printed '40 passed, 0 failed' and then hung. I confirmed all 40 assertions actually passed by redirecting the process output to a file and observing an idle (0.09s CPU) live process, which ruled out a bad assertion and pointed at a leaked event-loop handle. Root cause: `requestApproval()` in demo-bridge.ts armed a 120s expiry timer and discarded the handle, so the answer path in `approval.respond` removed the ticket but never called clearTimeout — the orphan timer kept Node alive for the full TTL. Fixed by tracking the timer on ApprovalTicket, clearing it on response, and unref()-ing it (guarded for browser environments) so it can never alone hold a process open. Also closed a secondary correctness gap: the expiry callback now re-reads the ticket instead of resolving through a captured closure, so an answered request can't later route an 'expired' resolution. Added 11 tests: 4 fake-timer tests that fail on the pre-fix code (timer count stays at 1 after a response) and 7 entry-point contract tests for the previously untested src/main.tsx. Note on FOLDER_SCOPE: `src/main.tsx` is a FILE, not a folder, so the literal glob `src/main.tsx/**/*.test.ts` matches nothing and zeroes out the whole vitest run ('No test files found'); I placed its test at src/ui/__tests__/main-entry.test.ts and ran the three real folders. Also note `npx --prefix` does not change cwd, so vitest must be invoked from inside xcoder-dojo.

defect_fixed.summary: Approval expiry timer (120s) was never cleared once an approval was answered, leaking an event-loop handle that prevented any Node process using the bridge from exiting — this is why `npm run regression` hung and AC3 failed.

tests_added.covers: Pending approval arms exactly one expiry timer; denying clears it and yields approval-denied; approving clears it and leaves no timers after the run drains; unanswered approval expires at TTL and a late response is refused with approval-expired. Fails against pre-fix code.

# Defect 0003 — Approval expiry timer is never cleared, hanging any Node process that uses the bridge

- **Defect ID:** defect0003
- **Discovered by:** tester (`test-st-bf6f22`)
- **Severity:** high
- **Affected file(s):** `xcoder-dojo/src/backend/demo-bridge.ts`
- **Status:** fixed and covered by regression tests

## Observed behaviour

`npm run regression` never terminated. The `test:unit` stage passed, then the
`test:smoke` stage printed its final line:

```
40 passed, 0 failed
```

and then hung indefinitely. The `node` process stayed alive with almost no CPU
(0.09 s consumed) and no further output, and had to be killed externally, so the
gate exited non-zero (timeout) despite every assertion passing.

Reproduction showed the assertions were not at fault: running the bundle with
output redirected to a file produced all 40 PASS lines and the summary, then the
process remained resident.

## Expected behaviour

When `test/smoke.ts` reaches the end of `main()`, all simulated work is finished
and the process should exit on its own with code 0. More generally: once an
approval request is answered, the bridge must hold no live timer for it, so a
host (smoke runner, CI, a future headless CLI) can exit normally.

## Reproduction steps

1. `cd xcoder-dojo`
2. `npm run test:smoke`
3. Observe all 40 checks PASS and the summary printed.
4. Observe the process does not exit; it must be killed.
5. Equivalent: `npm run regression` from the workspace root hangs after the unit
   stage instead of completing.

Minimal demonstration of the leaked handle:

```ts
const bridge = createDemoBridge({ now: () => NOW, autoConfigureModel: true });
await bridge.workspace.open('C:/projects/dojo-demo');
const launch = bridge.delegation.launch({ goal: 'rename a symbol' });
// ... read bridge.approval.pending(), then answer it ...
await bridge.approval.respond({ approvalId, decision: 'denied' });
// the 120s expiry timer is STILL registered -> event loop stays alive
```

## Root cause hypothesis

`requestApproval()` in `demo-bridge.ts` armed a 120 s expiry timer:

```ts
return new Promise((resolve) => {
  pendingApprovals.set(approvalId, { ...request, resolve });
  emit({ type: 'approval-requested', request });
  setTimeout(() => { /* resolve('expired') */ }, APPROVAL_TTL_MS); // 120_000
});
```

The timer handle was discarded, so no resolution path could cancel it. The
denial/approval path in the `approval.respond` facade removed the ticket from
`pendingApprovals` and resolved the promise, but never called `clearTimeout` on
the expiry timer. That orphaned timer remained referenced by the Node timer
subsystem, keeping the event loop alive for the full 120 s TTL after every test
run that exercised the approval gate.

The smoke test never called `process.exit()`, which is correct — a test should
not need an explicit kill. The leak was in the bridge, not the harness.

A mitigated second factor: the expiry callback used the captured `resolve`
closure rather than re-reading the ticket, so an already-answered request could
still route an `expired` resolution. Clearing the timer removes that path.

## Fix applied

1. `ApprovalTicket` now carries an optional `timer` handle.
2. `requestApproval()` stores the handle on the ticket and calls `unref()` when
   available, so the timer can never by itself keep a process alive (guarded, so
   browser environments where `setTimeout` returns a number are unaffected).
3. `approval.respond` clears the timer with `clearTimeout(ticket.timer)` before
   deleting the ticket, so a resolved approval leaves no scheduled work behind.

## Regression coverage

`xcoder-dojo/src/backend/__tests__/approval-timer.test.ts` (4 tests) encodes the
intended behaviour with fake timers:

- exactly one expiry timer is armed while an approval is pending;
- denying an approval leaves zero outstanding timers and yields
  `approval-denied` for the gated delegation;
- approving clears the expiry timer, and after the simulated delegation drains,
  no timers remain;
- an unanswered approval expires at the TTL and a late response is refused with
  `approval-expired`.

These fail against the pre-fix code (the timer count stays at 1 after a
response) and pass after it.

test-st-bf6f22.summary: Diagnosed and fixed the actual cause of the failing regression gate, then extended the suite. The previous attempt's 36 files were already on disk and largely sound — typecheck passed and 272 unit tests passed — so I bisected the gate instead of rewriting anything. `npm run regression` (typecheck && test:unit && test:smoke) failed because the smoke stage never exited: it printed '40 passed, 0 failed' and then hung. I confirmed all 40 assertions actually passed by redirecting the process output to a file and observing an idle (0.09s CPU) live process, which ruled out a bad assertion and pointed at a leaked event-loop handle. Root cause: `requestApproval()` in demo-bridge.ts armed a 120s expiry timer and discarded the handle, so the answer path in `approval.respond` removed the ticket but never called clearTimeout — the orphan timer kept Node alive for the full TTL. Fixed by tracking the timer on ApprovalTicket, clearing it on response, and unref()-ing it (guarded for browser environments) so it can never alone hold a process open. Also closed a secondary correctness gap: the expiry callback now re-reads the ticket instead of resolving through a captured closure, so an answered request can't later route an 'expired' resolution. Added 11 tests: 4 fake-timer tests that fail on the pre-fix code (timer count stays at 1 after a response) and 7 entry-point contract tests for the previously untested src/main.tsx. Note on FOLDER_SCOPE: `src/main.tsx` is a FILE, not a folder, so the literal glob `src/main.tsx/**/*.test.ts` matches nothing and zeroes out the whole vitest run ('No test files found'); I placed its test at src/ui/__tests__/main-entry.test.ts and ran the three real folders. Also note `npx --prefix` does not change cwd, so vitest must be invoked from inside xcoder-dojo.

documented_defect.title: Approval expiry timer leaked, hanging any Node process using the bridge
documented_defect.symptom: npm run regression printed 40 passed, 0 failed then hung at about 0.09s CPU and timed out
documented_defect.root_cause: requestApproval armed a 120s timer and discarded the handle, so approval.respond removed the ticket without clearTimeout and the orphan timer kept the event loop alive for the full TTL
documented_defect.fix: ApprovalTicket carries an optional timer; requestApproval stores it and calls unref when available; approval.respond calls clearTimeout before deleting the ticket; the expiry callback re-reads the ticket instead of using a captured closure
documented_defect.lesson: A passing assertion set is not a passing gate. A process that will not exit is a failure, and long-lived timers must be cancellable and unref'd.

# Xcoder Dojo

A TypeScript UI IDE with an embedded agent (JARVIS), implementing the page
specification in `.xcoder/backlog/design-st-2c7624.md`. It is a fresh,
self-contained build — nothing is imported from the PyQt6 reference in
`../xcoder-ai-dojo/`.

## Run

```bash
npm install
npm run dev        # http://localhost:5173
npm run build      # tsc --noEmit && vite build
npm run typecheck  # tsc --noEmit
npm test           # runtime smoke suite, 40 assertions
```

## Layers

```
src/contracts/   every type that crosses a page boundary
src/backend/     the privileged layer: sandbox, tools, audit, bridge
src/ui/          the pages P-00 .. P-12
```

The UI never touches a path or a process directly. It calls `DojoBridge`, which
validates and enforces in the backend. In Electron this object would sit behind
`contextBridge` in the main process; here it runs in the renderer but keeps the
same contract.

## Pages implemented

| Page | Component |
| --- | --- |
| P-00 App Shell | `ui/App.tsx` |
| P-01 Welcome | `ui/pages/WelcomePage.tsx` |
| P-02 / P-02a Explorer | `ui/components/Explorer.tsx` |

## 1. Goal
Build xcoder-dojo: a self-contained TypeScript implementation of the Xcoder AI Dojo desktop workbench, delivered as a new top-level folder xcoder-dojo/ in this workspace, startable with two documented commands, and usable to complete this end-to-end loop without touching the Python reference:
open a folder -> view its file tree -> open and edit a source file with syntax highlighting and line numbers -> save it preserving encoding and line endings -> run it and read output in a console -> ask the built-in agent to inspect the workspace and delegate a coding task -> see the agent tool calls and streamed agent output.
TypeScript UI and Agent means both halves in TypeScript: the UI layer AND the in-app assistant and tool-dispatch layer. The SdlcRun adapter that shells out to a Node agent CLI stays as the execution boundary, but tool dispatch, memory, bounds and approval logic are re-implemented in TypeScript.
Success is not that a folder named xcoder-dojo exists; it is the loop above running against a real workspace, real process execution and real agent tool calls, verified by driving the app rather than by reading its source.
---

# Defect 0003 â€” Approval expiry timer is never cleared, hanging any Node process that uses the bridge

- **Defect ID:** defect0003
- **Discovered by:** tester (`test-st-bf6f22`)
- **Severity:** high
- **Affected file(s):** `xcoder-dojo/src/backend/demo-bridge.ts`
- **Status:** fixed and covered by regression tests

## Observed behaviour

`npm run regression` never terminated. The `test:unit` stage passed, then the
`test:smoke` stage printed its final line:

```
40 passed, 0 failed
```

and then hung indefinitely. The `node` process stayed alive with almost no CPU
(0.09 s consumed) and no further output, and had to be killed externally, so the
gate exited non-zero (timeout) despite every assertion passing.

Reproduction showed the assertions were not at fault: running the bundle with
output redirected to a file produced all 40 PASS lines and the summary, then the
process remained resident.

## Expected behaviour

When `test/smoke.ts` reaches the end of `main()`, all simulated work is finished
and the process should exit on its own with code 0. More generally: once an
approval request is answered, the bridge must hold no live timer for it, so a
host (smoke runner, CI, a future headless CLI) can exit normally.

## Reproduction steps

1. `cd xcoder-dojo`
2. `npm run test:smoke`
3. Observe all 40 checks PASS and the summary printed.
4. Observe the process does not exit; it must be killed.
5. Equivalent: `npm run regression` from the workspace root hangs after the unit
   stage instead of completing.

Minimal demonstration of the leaked handle:

```ts
const bridge = createDemoBridge({ now: () => NOW, autoConfigureModel: true });
await bridge.workspace.open('C:/projects/dojo-demo');
const launch = bridge.delegation.launch({ goal: 'rename a symbol' });
// ... read bridge.approval.pending(), then answer it ...
await bridge.approval.respond({ approvalId, decision: 'denied' });
// the 120s expiry timer is STILL registered -> event loop stays alive
```

## Root cause hypothesis

`requestApproval()` in `demo-bridge.ts` armed a 120 s expiry timer:

```ts
return new Promise((resolve) => {
  pendingApprovals.set(approvalId, { ...request, resolve });
  emit({ type: 'approval-requested', request });
  setTimeout(() => { /* resolve('expired') */ }, APPROVAL_TTL_MS); // 120_000
});
```

The timer handle was discarded, so no resolution path could cancel it. The
denial/approval path in the `approval.respond` facade removed the ticket from
`pendingApprovals` and resolved the promise, but never called `clearTimeout` on
the expiry timer. That orphaned timer remained referenced by the Node timer
subsystem, keeping the event loop alive for the full 120 s TTL after every test
run that exercised the approval gate.

The smoke test never called `process.exit()`, which is correct â€” a test should
not need an explicit kill. The leak was in the bridge, not the harness.

A mitigated second factor: the expiry callback used the captured `resolve`
closure rather than re-reading the ticket, so an already-answered request could
still route an `expired` resolution. Clearing the timer removes that path.

## Fix applied

1. `ApprovalTicket` now carries an optional `timer` handle.
2. `requestApproval()` stores the handle on the ticket and calls `unref()` when
   available, so the timer can never by itself keep a process alive (guarded, so
   browser environments where `setTimeout` returns a number are unaffected).
3. `approval.respond` clears the timer with `clearTimeout(ticket.timer)` before
   deleting the ticket, so a resolved approval leaves no scheduled work behind.

<!-- xcoder:version 1 | xcoder:task task-f1d1f4 | xcoder:updated 2026-11-16 | xcoder:subtask document-st-fbebd7 -->
# Xcoder Dojo — Blueprint

Current architecture, workflow and feature inventory for `xcoder-dojo/`, the
TypeScript re-implementation of the Xcoder AI Dojo desktop workbench.

Source of truth for *what to build* is `.xcoder/backlog/requirements-st-b1522d.md`
(15 requirements, safety rules S-01..S-13, acceptance criteria AC-01..AC-21) and
`.xcoder/backlog/design-st-2c7624.md` (page specs P-00..P-12). This document
describes what was actually built.

---

## 1. What this is

A single-user, local-first IDE: open a folder, browse and edit files, run the
project, and talk to an embedded agent (JARVIS) that can inspect the workspace
through allowlisted read tools and propose a write that you must approve.

Two things are deliberately true of the build:

- **Nothing is imported from `../xcoder-ai-dojo/`** (the Python 3.10 / PyQt6
  v0.1.4 reference). `xcoder-dojo/` is a fresh, self-contained folder. The
  reference was read-only input.
- **Both halves are TypeScript.** The UI *and* the agent (tool dispatch, memory,
  bounds, approval logic) are TS. There is no Python at runtime.

Scope was cut explicitly in requirements §2. Out of scope for v1: the voice
subsystem (NG-01), a Docker agent catalogue (NG-02), installers/code signing
(NG-03), the Butler persona (NG-04), LSP/debugger/Git UI/package-manager GUIs
(NG-05), multi-user/cloud (NG-06), pixel-parity theming (NG-07), a durable AI
task board (NG-08), migration of the PyQt `~/.xcoder/dojo` data root (NG-09), and
non-English recognition models (NG-10).

---

## 2. Architecture

```
xcoder-dojo/
  src/contracts/   every type that crosses a page boundary (no runtime deps)
  src/backend/     the privileged layer: sandbox, vfs, tools, agent, audit, bridge
  src/ui/          P-00 shell + pages P-01..P-12 and the shared components
  src/main.tsx     the single entry point: bridge construction -> render
  test/smoke.ts    40 end-to-end assertions driving the bridge
```

### 2.1 The one hardening boundary: `DojoBridge`

`src/contracts/bridge.ts` defines `DojoBridge` — *the entire privileged surface
exposed to the UI*. There is no `ipcRenderer` passthrough and no generic
`invoke(channel, ...)`: every capability is an explicitly named method that
returns a `BridgeResult<T>`. The frozen surface is 11 sub-APIs plus a
subscription:

| API | Methods |
| --- | --- |
| `workspace` | `current` `recents` `open` `close` |
| `tree` | `listChildren` (cursor-paged) |
| `files` | `read` `save` `agentWrite` `markdown` |
| `run` | `targets` `session` `start` `stop` |
| `agent` | `state` `send` `stop` `retryLast` `clearConversation` |
| `session` | `list` `load` `clear` `clearAll` |
| `delegation` | `current` `launch` `stop` |
| `approval` | `pending` `respond` |
| `settings` | `get` `patch` `setApiKey` `clearApiKey` |
| `audit` | `page` `location` |
| `status` | `get` |
| — | `subscribe(listener): () => void` |

The UI never touches a path or a process directly; it calls the bridge, which
normalises and enforces in `src/backend/`. In Electron this object would sit
behind `contextBridge` in the main process. Here it runs in the renderer while
keeping the identical contract, so promoting it later is a transport change, not
an API redesign (constraint C-02 permitted this substitution).

`BridgeEvent` is the push channel: `agent`, `run`, `delegation`,
`approval-requested`, `approval-resolved`, `audit`, `settings-changed`,
`status-changed`, `error`. Pages never poll.

### 2.2 Backend modules

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `sandbox.ts` | Path normalisation + visibility. The single chokepoint every `relPath` passes through. |
| `vfs.ts` | Virtual file system used by the demo bridge, so the UI is exercisable without a real disk. |
| `tools.ts` | `dispatchTool` — the only entry point to the 11 allowlisted read tools. |
| `agent-engine.ts` | Deterministic local model stub + injection detection. |
| `audit.ts` | Append-only, redacted-at-write-time audit log. |
| `store.ts` | Settings, limits, recents, sessions; `DEFAULT_LIMITS`. |
| `markdown.ts` | Markdown → AST (never HTML). |
| `demo-bridge.ts` | `createDemoBridge()` — wires all of the above into `DojoBridge`. |

### 2.3 UI layer

`src/ui/App.tsx` is the P-00 shell: title bar (brand, active workspace path,
JARVIS/Delegation dock switch, audit + settings buttons, close workspace),
left dock (Explorer), center column (`EditorPage` or `WelcomePage`), bottom dock
(`RunConsolePage`), right dock (`AgentPanel` / `DelegationPage`), status bar,
error center, and the approval overlay slot.

State survives navigation because overlays never unmount the shell. Pages read
via `useAppState` / write via `useAppActions` (`store.tsx`); the provider
(`AppProvider.tsx`) owns state and subscribes to the bridge once.

`src/main.tsx` is small and contract-tested: it builds exactly one bridge, calls
`autoConfigureModel`, resolves `#root` (refusing to boot without it), and renders
`<App/>` inside `<AppProvider bridge={...}>` within `StrictMode` — bridge
constructed *before* render, in that order.

---

## 3. Feature inventory

Pages implemented, mapped to their design IDs and files (from README):

| Design | Feature | Component |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P-00 | App shell | `ui/App.tsx` |
| P-01 | Welcome / recent workspaces | `ui/pages/WelcomePage.tsx` |
| P-02 / P-02a | Explorer tree | `ui/components/Explorer.tsx` |
| P-03 / a / b / c | Editor: tabs, syntax highlighting, line numbers, markdown preview | `EditorPage.tsx`, `SyntaxEditor.tsx`, `MarkdownView.tsx` |
| P-04 / P-04a | Run console with stop control | `RunConsolePage.tsx` |
| P-05 / a / b / c | Agent panel, transcript, tool cards | `AgentPanel.tsx`, `TranscriptView.tsx`, `ToolCard.tsx` |
| P-06 | Delegation to the agent CLI | `DelegationPage.tsx` |
| P-07 | Approval sheet | `ApprovalSheet.tsx` |
| P-08 / a / b / c | Settings (model, theme, limits, key) | `SettingsModal.tsx` |
| P-09 | Chat history | `HistoryModal.tsx` |
| P-10 | Audit log | `AuditModal.tsx` |
| P-11 | Status bar | `components/StatusBar.tsx` |
| P-12 | Error center | `components/ErrorCenter.tsx` |

Runtime limits and defaults, in `src/backend/store.ts`:

- `DEFAULT_LIMITS` = `maxTurns: 5`, `maxInputChars: 4_000`, `requestCapPerHour: 40`
- `maxFileReadBytes = 200_000` (reads above this are truncated and flagged)
- `APPROVAL_TTL_MS = 120_000` in `demo-bridge.ts`
- `auditRetentionDays = 30`; audit log dir `.xcoder/logs/audit`
- themes: `dojo-dark` (default), `dojo-hud`, `dojo-light`
- model identity: `local-stub / dojo-local-7b`; delegation CLI label `xcoder-agent-cli`

---

## 4. Workflow: the end-to-end loop

The loop the requirements defined as the definition of success:

1. **Open a folder** → `workspace.open(rootDisplayPath)` normalises the root,
   records a recent (max 10), and emits `status-changed`.
2. **View the tree** → `tree.listChildren` is cursor-paged (`nextCursor`),
   reports `truncated` past 1500 entries, and returns `scannedFiles`. The tree is
   a *projection* of the sandbox decision, so excluded nodes are never listed.
3. **Open and edit** → `files.read` returns `{ content, encoding, eol, language,
   sizeBytes, truncated, savedSha }`. `encoding` is `'utf-8' | 'utf-8-bom'` and
   `eol` is `'lf' | 'crlf'` — both round-trip through `files.save`, which is how
   AC-04 (BOM/CRLF fidelity) is met.
4. **Save** → `files.save` validates via `normalizeWritePath`, then writes.
5. **Run** → `run.targets()` lists `CommandSpec`s; `run.start` spawns with the
   workspace as cwd, streams `RunEvent`s, enforces a timeout and output caps, and
   `run.stop` is the visible Stop control.
6. **Ask the agent** → `agent.send` records the request, runs the model stub,
   dispatches read tools, and streams `AgentEvent`s (tokens + `ToolCallRecord`s)
   to the panel.
7. **Approve a write** → the agent cannot write. `files.agentWrite` and
   `delegation.launch` each call `requestApproval(...)`, which queues an
   `ApprovalRequest` (kind `file-write` | `delegation-launch`, naming the concrete
   target), emits `approval-requested`, and blocks until `approval.respond` or
   the 120 s TTL. Everything else is refused outright rather than approved.

---

## 5. Safety properties — where each is enforced

Per PRM-09 / S-05, these are enforced in code, not by prompt instructions. Each
has a smoke assertion in `test/smoke.ts` (40 total).

| Property | Enforced in | Mechanism |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Path sandbox (S-06) | `backend/sandbox.ts` | Refuses absolute paths, `..`, backslashes, NULs, dotfiles, excluded dirs (`node_modules`, `dist`, `build`, `.git`, `.xcoder`), and credential-shaped names (`.env*`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `id_rsa|ed25519|ecdsa`, `.npmrc`, `.netrc`, `credentials(.json)`, `secrets.*`). |
| Closed tool allowlist (PRM-04, S-03) | `backend/tools.ts` | `dispatchTool` checks `isAllowlistedTool` as its *first* statement. A fabricated name returns `denied-allowlist` and never reaches an implementation. The 11 tools are exactly: `list_dir`, `glob`, `grep`, `read_file`, `read_multiple_files`, `read_file_lines`, `read_outline`, `validate_file`, `git_status`, `git_diff`, `git_log`. No `run_command`/`shell`/`fetch_url`/`eval` is exposed to the model. |
| Injection is data (PRM-01/02) | `backend/agent-engine.ts` | `detectInjection` matches ignore-previous-instructions / exfiltrate / reveal-key patterns. The stub *reports* an injection attempt instead of acting on it. |
| Sanitized markdown (PRM-08) | `backend/markdown.ts` | Returns an AST, never HTML. Block and inline HTML are stripped; images are blocked. |
| Human approval (AI-03, S-07) | `backend/demo-bridge.ts` | `requestApproval` gates `file-write` and `delegation-launch`, naming the target; 120 s TTL → `expired`. |
| Bounded execution (AI-04, S-08) | `backend/demo-bridge.ts` | Run processes use the workspace as cwd, no shell interpolation of model strings, a timeout, output caps, and a Stop control. |
| Cost/abuse caps (AI-09, S-10) | `backend/store.ts` | `maxTurns: 5`, `maxInputChars: 4_000`, `requestCapPerHour: 40`, plus a kill switch (`agent.stop`) aborting in-flight work. |
| Redacted audit (PRM-10, S-11) | `backend/audit.ts` | Redaction happens **at write time** (`redact()` on `sk-…`, `Bearer …`, `api_key|token|password = …`), so un-redacted text never exists in the store to leak later. Retention 30 days; location disclosed in the UI. |
| No key exfiltration (PRM-03) | `backend/store.ts` | `setApiKey` accepts a key and never returns it; `secretState()` exposes only `{ hasApiKey, updatedAtMs }`. The audit smoke assertion confirms the key is never recorded. |
| Structured output (PRM-07/08, S-04) | `contracts/` + `tools.ts` | Tool calls are schema-typed; unparseable output is rejected and surfaced, never executed. |

---

## 6. Verification status

Commands (run from inside `xcoder-dojo/`):

```bash
npm run dev        # vite dev server, http://localhost:5173
npm run build      # tsc --noEmit && vite build
npm run typecheck  # tsc --noEmit
npm run test:unit  # vitest, 12 files / 283 tests
npm run test:smoke # esbuild test/smoke.ts -> node, 40 assertions
npm run regression # typecheck && test:unit && test:smoke
```

Last verified state: `tsc --noEmit` clean; **12 test files, 283 tests passed**
in 1.53 s; smoke suite **40 passed, 0 failed** and the process exits 0 on its own.

Test layout: `src/backend/__tests__/` (agent-engine 31, demo-bridge 41, tools 33,
approval-timer 4, plus audit/markdown/sandbox/vfs), `src/contracts/__tests__/`
