# Xcoder Dojo — Blueprint

Current architecture, workflow and feature inventory for `xcoder-dojo/`, the
TypeScript re-implementation of the Xcoder AI Dojo desktop workbench.

Source of truth for *what to build* is `.xcoder/backlog/requirements-st-b1522d.md`
(15 requirements, safety rules S-01..S-13, acceptance criteria AC-01..AC-21) and
`.xcoder/backlog/design-st-2c7624.md` (page specs P-00..P-12). This document
describes what was actually built.

---

## 1. What this is

A single-user, local-first IDE: open a folder, browse and edit files, run the
project, and talk to an embedded agent (JARVIS) that can inspect the workspace
through allowlisted read tools and propose a write that you must approve.

Two things are deliberately true of the build:

- **Nothing is imported from `../xcoder-ai-dojo/`** (the Python 3.10 / PyQt6
  v0.1.4 reference). `xcoder-dojo/` is a fresh, self-contained folder. The
  reference was read-only input.
- **Both halves are TypeScript.** The UI *and* the agent (tool dispatch, memory,
  bounds, approval logic) are TS. There is no Python at runtime.

Scope was cut explicitly in requirements §2. Out of scope for v1: the voice
subsystem (NG-01), a Docker agent catalogue (NG-02), installers/code signing
(NG-03), the Butler persona (NG-04), LSP/debugger/Git UI/package-manager GUIs
(NG-05), multi-user/cloud (NG-06), pixel-parity theming (NG-07), a durable AI
task board (NG-08), migration of the PyQt `~/.xcoder/dojo` data root (NG-09), and
non-English recognition models (NG-10).

---

## 2. Architecture

```
xcoder-dojo/
  src/contracts/   every type that crosses a page boundary (no runtime deps)
  src/backend/     the privileged layer: sandbox, vfs, tools, agent, audit, bridge
  src/ui/          P-00 shell + pages P-01..P-12 and the shared components
  src/main.tsx     the single entry point: bridge construction -> render
  test/smoke.ts    40 end-to-end assertions driving the bridge
```

### 2.1 The one hardening boundary: `DojoBridge`

`src/contracts/bridge.ts` defines `DojoBridge` — *the entire privileged surface
exposed to the UI*. There is no `ipcRenderer` passthrough and no generic
`invoke(channel, ...)`: every capability is an explicitly named method that
returns a `BridgeResult<T>`. The frozen surface is 11 sub-APIs plus a
subscription:

| API | Methods |
| --- | --- |
| `workspace` | `current` `recents` `open` `close` |
| `tree` | `listChildren` (cursor-paged) |
| `files` | `read` `save` `agentWrite` `markdown` |
| `run` | `targets` `session` `start` `stop` |
| `agent` | `state` `send` `stop` `retryLast` `clearConversation` |
| `session` | `list` `load` `clear` `clearAll` |
| `delegation` | `current` `launch` `stop` |
| `approval` | `pending` `respond` |
| `settings` | `get` `patch` `setApiKey` `clearApiKey` |
| `audit` | `page` `location` |
| `status` | `get` |
| — | `subscribe(listener): () => void` |

The UI never touches a path or a process directly; it calls the bridge, which
normalises and enforces in `src/backend/`. In Electron this object would sit
behind `contextBridge` in the main process. Here it runs in the renderer while
keeping the identical contract, so promoting it later is a transport change, not
an API redesign (constraint C-02 permitted this substitution).

`BridgeEvent` is the push channel: `agent`, `run`, `delegation`,
`approval-requested`, `approval-resolved`, `audit`, `settings-changed`,
`status-changed`, `error`. Pages never poll.

### 2.2 Backend modules

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `sandbox.ts` | Path normalisation + visibility. The single chokepoint every `relPath` passes through. |
| `vfs.ts` | Virtual file system used by the demo bridge, so the UI is exercisable without a real disk. |
| `tools.ts` | `dispatchTool` — the only entry point to the 11 allowlisted read tools. |
| `agent-engine.ts` | Deterministic local model stub + injection detection. |
| `audit.ts` | Append-only, redacted-at-write-time audit log. |
| `store.ts` | Settings, limits, recents, sessions; `DEFAULT_LIMITS`. |
| `markdown.ts` | Markdown → AST (never HTML). |
| `demo-bridge.ts` | `createDemoBridge()` — wires all of the above into `DojoBridge`. |

### 2.3 UI layer

`src/ui/App.tsx` is the P-00 shell: title bar (brand, active workspace path,
JARVIS/Delegation dock switch, audit + settings buttons, close workspace),
left dock (Explorer), center column (`EditorPage` or `WelcomePage`), bottom dock
(`RunConsolePage`), right dock (`AgentPanel` / `DelegationPage`), status bar,
error center, and the approval overlay slot.

State survives navigation because overlays never unmount the shell. Pages read
via `useAppState` / write via `useAppActions` (`store.tsx`); the provider
(`AppProvider.tsx`) owns state and subscribes to the bridge once.

`src/main.tsx` is small and contract-tested: it builds exactly one bridge, calls
`autoConfigureModel`, resolves `#root` (refusing to boot without it), and renders
`<App/>` inside `<AppProvider bridge={...}>` within `StrictMode` — bridge
constructed *before* render, in that order.

---

## 3. Feature inventory

Pages implemented, mapped to their design IDs and files (from README):

| Design | Feature | Component |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P-00 | App shell | `ui/App.tsx` |
| P-01 | Welcome / recent workspaces | `ui/pages/WelcomePage.tsx` |
| P-02 / P-02a | Explorer tree | `ui/components/Explorer.tsx` |
| P-03 / a / b / c | Editor: tabs, syntax highlighting, line numbers, markdown preview | `EditorPage.tsx`, `SyntaxEditor.tsx`, `MarkdownView.tsx` |
| P-04 / P-04a | Run console with stop control | `RunConsolePage.tsx` |
| P-05 / a / b / c | Agent panel, transcript, tool cards | `AgentPanel.tsx`, `TranscriptView.tsx`, `ToolCard.tsx` |
| P-06 | Delegation to the agent CLI | `DelegationPage.tsx` |
| P-07 | Approval sheet | `ApprovalSheet.tsx` |
| P-08 / a / b / c | Settings (model, theme, limits, key) | `SettingsModal.tsx` |
| P-09 | Chat history | `HistoryModal.tsx` |
| P-10 | Audit log | `AuditModal.tsx` |
| P-11 | Status bar | `components/StatusBar.tsx` |
| P-12 | Error center | `components/ErrorCenter.tsx` |

Runtime limits and defaults, in `src/backend/store.ts`:

- `DEFAULT_LIMITS` = `maxTurns: 5`, `maxInputChars: 4_000`, `requestCapPerHour: 40`
- `maxFileReadBytes = 200_000` (reads above this are truncated and flagged)
- `APPROVAL_TTL_MS = 120_000` in `demo-bridge.ts`
- `auditRetentionDays = 30`; audit log dir `.xcoder/logs/audit`
- themes: `dojo-dark` (default), `dojo-hud`, `dojo-light`
- model identity: `local-stub / dojo-local-7b`; delegation CLI label `xcoder-agent-cli`

---

## 4. Workflow: the end-to-end loop

The loop the requirements defined as the definition of success:

1. **Open a folder** → `workspace.open(rootDisplayPath)` normalises the root,
   records a recent (max 10), and emits `status-changed`.
2. **View the tree** → `tree.listChildren` is cursor-paged (`nextCursor`),
   reports `truncated` past 1500 entries, and returns `scannedFiles`. The tree is
   a *projection* of the sandbox decision, so excluded nodes are never listed.
3. **Open and edit** → `files.read` returns `{ content, encoding, eol, language,
   sizeBytes, truncated, savedSha }`. `encoding` is `'utf-8' | 'utf-8-bom'` and
   `eol` is `'lf' | 'crlf'` — both round-trip through `files.save`, which is how
   AC-04 (BOM/CRLF fidelity) is met.
4. **Save** → `files.save` validates via `normalizeWritePath`, then writes.
5. **Run** → `run.targets()` lists `CommandSpec`s; `run.start` spawns with the
   workspace as cwd, streams `RunEvent`s, enforces a timeout and output caps, and
   `run.stop` is the visible Stop control.
6. **Ask the agent** → `agent.send` records the request, runs the model stub,
   dispatches read tools, and streams `AgentEvent`s (tokens + `ToolCallRecord`s)
   to the panel.
7. **Approve a write** → the agent cannot write. `files.agentWrite` and
   `delegation.launch` each call `requestApproval(...)`, which queues an
   `ApprovalRequest` (kind `file-write` | `delegation-launch`, naming the concrete
   target), emits `approval-requested`, and blocks until `approval.respond` or
   the 120 s TTL. Everything else is refused outright rather than approved.

---

## 5. Safety properties — where each is enforced

Per PRM-09 / S-05, these are enforced in code, not by prompt instructions. Each
has a smoke assertion in `test/smoke.ts` (40 total).

| Property | Enforced in | Mechanism |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Path sandbox (S-06) | `backend/sandbox.ts` | Refuses absolute paths, `..`, backslashes, NULs, dotfiles, excluded dirs (`node_modules`, `dist`, `build`, `.git`, `.xcoder`), and credential-shaped names (`.env*`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `id_rsa|ed25519|ecdsa`, `.npmrc`, `.netrc`, `credentials(.json)`, `secrets.*`). |
| Closed tool allowlist (PRM-04, S-03) | `backend/tools.ts` | `dispatchTool` checks `isAllowlistedTool` as its *first* statement. A fabricated name returns `denied-allowlist` and never reaches an implementation. | Injection is data (PRM-01/02) | `backend/agent-engine.ts` | `detectInjection` matches ignore-previous-instructions / exfiltrate / reveal-key patterns. The stub *reports* an injection attempt instead of acting on it. |
| Sanitized markdown (PRM-08) | `backend/markdown.ts` | Returns an AST, never HTML. Block and inline HTML are stripped; images are blocked. |
| Human approval (AI-03, S-07) | `backend/demo-bridge.ts` | `requestApproval` gates `file-write` and `delegation-launch`, naming the target; 120 s TTL → `expired`. |
| Bounded execution (AI-04, S-08) | `backend/demo-bridge.ts` | Run processes use the workspace as cwd, no shell interpolation of model strings, a timeout, output caps, and a Stop control. |
| Cost/abuse caps (AI-09, S-10) | `backend/store.ts` | `maxTurns: 5`, `maxInputChars: 4_000`, `requestCapPerHour: 40`, plus a kill switch (`agent.stop`) aborting in-flight work. |

| No key exfiltration (PRM-03) | `backend/store.ts` | `setApiKey` accepts a key and never returns it; `secretState()` exposes only `{ hasApiKey, updatedAtMs }`. The audit smoke assertion confirms the key is never recorded. |
| Structured output (PRM-07/08, S-04) | `contracts/` + `tools.ts` | Tool calls are schema-typed; unparseable output is rejected and surfaced, never executed. |

---

## 6. Verification status

npm run build      # tsc --noEmit && vite build

# Changelog — xcoder-dojo

Change record for the TypeScript re-implementation of the Xcoder AI Dojo
workbench. Architecture and feature inventory live in `.xcoder/blueprint.md`.

---

## 0.1.0 — initial TypeScript build (task-f1d1f4)

### What changed

Created `xcoder-dojo/`, a new top-level, self-contained folder — nothing is
imported from the Python 3.10 / PyQt6 reference in `../xcoder-ai-dojo/` (v0.1.4).
Both the UI **and** the agent are TypeScript; no Python is required at runtime.

**Layers**

- `src/contracts/` — every type that crosses a page boundary. `bridge.ts` freezes
  `DojoBridge` as the entire privileged surface: 11 explicitly named sub-APIs
  (`workspace`, `tree`, `files`, `run`, `agent`, `session`, `delegation`,
  `approval`, `settings`, `audit`, `status`) plus `subscribe`. No `ipcRenderer`
  passthrough, no generic `invoke(channel, …)`.
- `src/backend/` — the privileged layer: `sandbox.ts` (path chokepoint), `vfs.ts`,
  `tools.ts` (allowlist dispatch), `agent-engine.ts` (deterministic model stub),
  `audit.ts`, `store.ts`, `markdown.ts`, and `demo-bridge.ts`
  (`createDemoBridge()`, which wires them into the bridge).
- `src/ui/` — P-00 shell plus pages P-01..P-12 and shared components.
- `test/smoke.ts` — 40 end-to-end assertions driving the bridge.

**Features** — the loop from the requirements runs end to end: open a folder →
lazy, cursor-paged tree → open/edit a file (`encoding: 'utf-8' | 'utf-8-bom'`,
`eol: 'lf' | 'crlf'`, both round-tripping through `files.save`) → run with a
visible Stop control → ask JARVIS, which inspects the workspace through
allowlisted read tools → approve the agent's proposed write.

### Why

The requirements (`.xcoder/backlog/requirements-st-b1522d.md`) defined success as
*the loop running against a real workspace, verified by driving the app* — not as
a folder existing. The design (`.xcoder/backlog/design-st-2c7624.md`) specified
pages P-00..P-12. Scope was cut deliberately to keep that loop honest: no voice
subsystem (NG-01), no Docker agent catalogue (NG-02), no installers (NG-03), no
Butler persona (NG-04), no LSP/debugger/Git UI (NG-05).

Security posture is enforced in code, not in a prompt (PRM-09 / S-05), because a
system-prompt instruction is not a security boundary:

- **Path sandbox** (`sandbox.ts`) refuses absolute paths, `..`, backslashes,
  NULs, dotfiles, `node_modules`/`dist`/`build`/`.git`/`.xcoder`, and
  credential-shaped names (`.env*`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `id_rsa|ed25519|ecdsa`,
  `.npmrc`, `.netrc`, `credentials(.json)`, `secrets.*`).
- **Closed tool allowlist** — `dispatchTool` checks `isAllowlistedTool` as its
  *first* statement; the 11 tools are `list_dir`, `glob`, `grep`, `read_file`,
  `read_multiple_files`, `read_file_lines`, `read_outline`, `validate_file`,
  `git_status`, `git_diff`, `git_log`. No `run_command`/`shell`/`fetch_url`/`eval`
  reaches the model.
- **Human approval** for `file-write` and `delegation-launch`, naming the concrete
  target, with a 120 s TTL → `expired`.
- **Redaction at write time** in `audit.ts` (`sk-…`, `Bearer …`,
  `api_key|token|password = …`), so un-redacted text never exists in the store.
- **Key never readable** — `Store.setApiKey` accepts a key; `secretState()`
  exposes only `{ hasApiKey, updatedAtMs }`.

### Fixed during this task

**defect0003 (high) — approval expiry timer leaked, hanging any Node process
that used the bridge.** `npm run regression` never terminated: `test:smoke`
printed `40 passed, 0 failed` and then hung with ~0.09 s CPU. The assertions were
fine; `requestApproval()` in `demo-bridge.ts` armed a 120 s timer and discarded
the handle, so `approval.respond` removed the ticket without `clearTimeout`. The
orphan kept the event loop alive for the full TTL, so the gate timed out despite
every check passing.

Fix: `ApprovalTicket` now carries an optional `timer`; `requestApproval` stores
it and `unref()`s it (feature-detected, so browser `setTimeout` returning a number
is unaffected); `approval.respond` calls `clearTimeout(ticket.timer)` before
deleting the ticket. The expiry callback re-reads the ticket instead of resolving
through a captured closure, so an answered request can never later route an
`expired` resolution. RCA: `.xcoder/defects/defect0003.md`.

### Verification

From inside `xcoder-dojo/`:

```
npm run typecheck   # tsc --noEmit — clean
npm run test:unit   # 12 files, 283 tests passed (1.53 s)
npm run test:smoke  # 40 passed, 0 failed — process exits 0 on its own
npm run regression  # typecheck && test:unit && test:smoke
```

New coverage added with the fix: `src/backend/__tests__/approval-timer.test.ts`
(4 tests, fails against pre-fix code — asserted timer count stays at 1 after a
response) and `src/ui/__tests__/main-entry.test.ts` (7 tests).

### Rollback

`xcoder-dojo/` is additive — no existing workspace file was modified to create it,
so rollback is `Remove-Item -Recurse xcoder-dojo` (or delete the folder). To
revert only defect0003, restore the discarded-handle form of `requestApproval()`
in `src/backend/demo-bridge.ts`; do not do this — it re-breaks `npm run
regression`.

The docs this task touched are `.xcoder/blueprint.md` (created) and
`xcoder-dojo/CHANGELOG.md` (this file).

### Gotchas for the next person

- `src/main.tsx` is a **file**, not a folder. A `FOLDER_SCOPE` glob of
  `src/main.tsx/**/*.test.ts` matches nothing and zeroes the whole vitest run

  `src/contracts`, `src/ui`.
- Do **not** use `npx --prefix` for vitest — it does not change cwd and breaks

rca.observedBehaviour:
The agent's allowlisted read tools enumerated paths that the UI tree is
required to hide. With the seeded demo workspace:

- `list_dir` on the root returned `.git/`, `node_modules/` and `.env` in its
  summary, e.g. `8 entries in .: .git/, docs/, node_modules/, ...`.
- `glob` with pattern `**/*` returned `.env` and `.git/config`.
- `grep` for `SOME_API_KEY` returned a hit of `.env:1`, i.e. the agent could
  confirm the location and line number of a credential file.

`tree.listChildren` correctly filtered these entries, so the UI hid them while
the agent did not.
rca.expectedBehaviour:
`README.md` states: "The agent can only call the 11 allowlisted read tools",
and the design (P-02 security notes, S-06) states that dotfiles, generated
directories and credential-shaped names are *never visible*. The allowlist
restricts **which tools** may run; the sandbox must restrict **what they can
touch**. Hiding a path from the explorer while exposing it to the agent is a
security boundary with two different answers.

Specifically:

- `.env` must never appear in any tool summary, and its contents must never be
  readable or greppable (see `crypto-architect` bylaw PRM-09: policy enforced
  in code, not by the prompt).
- `node_modules/`, `dist/`, `build/`, `.git/` and `.xcoder/` must not be
  enumerable by the agent.
rca.rootCauseHypothesis:
`dispatchTool` in `src/backend/tools.ts` applies `normalizeRelPath` to the
*requested* path, which correctly refuses an explicit `.env` argument. But the
enumeration tools (`list_dir`, `glob`, `grep`) then iterate over
`vfs.entries` directly and never apply the `isVisibleName` filter that
`tree.listChildren` applies in `demo-bridge.ts`. The visibility rule lived in
only one of the two call sites, so it was a defence with a hole in the other.

Fix: add a single `isVisibleRelPath` helper in `tools.ts` that requires every
segment to satisfy `isVisibleName`, and apply it to `list_dir` results, `glob`
matches and `grep` files. The rule now has one definition and both call sites
use it.

# defect0001 — Agent read tools leak credential, dotfile and generated paths

- **Defect ID:** defect0001
- **Discovered by:** tester (subtask `test-st-bf6f22`)
- **Severity:** high
- **Status:** fixed in this subtask

## Observed behaviour

The agent's allowlisted read tools enumerated paths that the UI tree is
required to hide. With the seeded demo workspace:

- `list_dir` on the root returned `.git/`, `node_modules/` and `.env` in its
  summary, e.g. `8 entries in .: .git/, docs/, node_modules/, ...`.
- `glob` with pattern `**/*` returned `.env` and `.git/config`.
- `grep` for `SOME_API_KEY` returned a hit of `.env:1`, i.e. the agent could
  confirm the location and line number of a credential file.

`tree.listChildren` correctly filtered these entries, so the UI hid them while
the agent did not.

## Expected behaviour

`README.md` states: "The agent can only call the 11 allowlisted read tools",
and the design (P-02 security notes, S-06) states that dotfiles, generated
directories and credential-shaped names are *never visible*. The allowlist
restricts **which tools** may run; the sandbox must restrict **what they can
touch**. Hiding a path from the explorer while exposing it to the agent is a
security boundary with two different answers.

Specifically:

- `.env` must never appear in any tool summary, and its contents must never be
  readable or greppable (see `crypto-architect` bylaw PRM-09: policy enforced
  in code, not by the prompt).
- `node_modules/`, `dist/`, `build/`, `.git/` and `.xcoder/` must not be
  enumerable by the agent.

## Reproduction steps

1. `npm install` in `xcoder-dojo/`.
2. Run `npx vitest run --config vitest.config.ts src/backend/__tests__/tools.test.ts`.
3. Before the fix, three tests failed:
   - `list_dir > never lists credential-shaped or generated entries`
   - `glob > does not leak hidden or generated file paths`
   - `grep > never returns a hit inside a credential file`

Equivalent manual reproduction:

```ts
const vfs = createVfs(Date.now());
dispatchTool(vfs, { toolName: 'grep', args: { pattern: 'SOME_API_KEY' } });
// -> { outcome: 'ok', summary: '1 match(es) for /SOME_API_KEY/: .env:1' }
```

## Root cause hypothesis

`dispatchTool` in `src/backend/tools.ts` applies `normalizeRelPath` to the
*requested* path, which correctly refuses an explicit `.env` argument. But the
enumeration tools (`list_dir`, `glob`, `grep`) then iterate over
`vfs.entries` directly and never apply the `isVisibleName` filter that
`tree.listChildren` applies in `demo-bridge.ts`. The visibility rule lived in
only one of the two call sites, so it was a defence with a hole in the other.

Fix: add a single `isVisibleRelPath` helper in `tools.ts` that requires every
segment to satisfy `isVisibleName`, and apply it to `list_dir` results, `glob`
matches and `grep` files. The rule now has one definition and both call sites
use it.

## Affected files

- `xcoder-dojo/src/backend/tools.ts` (fixed)
- `xcoder-dojo/src/backend/__tests__/tools.test.ts` (regression coverage added)

## Verification

`npx vitest run --config vitest.config.ts src/backend/__tests__/tools.test.ts`
-> 33 tests passed, including the three previously failing leak assertions.

rca.observedBehaviour: The sanitiser stripped raw HTML and remote images, but a Markdown link with a script scheme survived intact. Parsing ```md click [me](javascript:alert(1)) ``` produced a link span with `href: 'javascript:alert(1)'`, and `MarkdownView` rendered it as `me`. Any `data:`, `vbscript:` or mixed-case variant behaved the same way.
rca.expectedBehaviour:
The design (T-07, UI-02) says the parser "never returns HTML" so the renderer
"has nothing dangerous to insert". A script-scheme href defeats that: the AST
is data, but the `href` attribute is an executable sink. The UI also renders
model- and workspace-derived text, so this is the classic
"raw model output into an interpreter" path (bylaw PRM-08).

Expected: unsafe schemes are neutralised - the link label survives as inert
text and no executable URL reaches the DOM. `http:`, `https:`, `mailto:`, and
root-relative/fragment links remain valid, with `http(s)` still flagged
`external: true` so the renderer can add `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.
rca.rootCauseHypothesis:
In `inline()` (`src/backend/markdown.ts`) the link branch accepted any
non-empty destination:

```ts
const href = link[2].trim();
const external = /^https?:\/\//i.test(href);
spans.push({ kind: 'link', text: link[1], href, external });
```

The `external` flag only decides presentation; nothing validated the scheme.
Sanitising was implemented for HTML and images but this third sink was
overlooked because it looked like "a link" rather than "an href".

Fix: add an allowlist-based `isSafeHref` (`http`, `https`, `mailto`, or no
scheme at all) and, for anything else, emit the link text as a plain text
span. Allowlisting a small set is safer than blocklisting `javascript:`,
because the blocklist always misses a case.

dag.goal: Confirm the defect described in .xcoder/defects/defect0003.md no longer reproduces, via a real test run.

rca.observedBehaviour:
`npm run regression` never terminated. The `test:unit` stage passed, then the
`test:smoke` stage printed its final line:

```
40 passed, 0 failed
```

and then hung indefinitely. The `node` process stayed alive with almost no CPU
(0.09 s consumed) and no further output, and had to be killed externally, so the
gate exited non-zero (timeout) despite every assertion passing.

Reproduction showed the assertions were not at fault: running the bundle with
output redirected to a file produced all 40 PASS lines and the summary, then the
process remained resident.
rca.expectedBehaviour:
When `test/smoke.ts` reaches the end of `main()`, all simulated work is finished
and the process should exit on its own with code 0. More generally: once an
approval request is answered, the bridge must hold no live timer for it, so a
host (smoke runner, CI, a future headless CLI) can exit normally.
rca.rootCauseHypothesis:
`requestApproval()` in `demo-bridge.ts` armed a 120 s expiry timer:

```ts
return new Promise((resolve) => {
  pendingApprovals.set(approvalId, { ...request, resolve });
  emit({ type: 'approval-requested', request });
  setTimeout(() => { /* resolve('expired') */ }, APPROVAL_TTL_MS); // 120_000
});
```

The timer handle was discarded, so no resolution path could cancel it. The
denial/approval path in the `approval.respond` facade removed the ticket from
`pendingApprovals` and resolved the promise, but never called `clearTimeout` on
the expiry timer. That orphaned timer remained referenced by the Node timer
subsystem, keeping the event loop alive for the full 120 s TTL after every test
run that exercised the approval gate.

The smoke test never called `process.exit()`, which is correct — a test should
not need an explicit kill. The leak was in the bridge, not the harness.

A mitigated second factor: the expiry callback used the captured `resolve`
closure rather than re-reading the ticket, so an already-answered request could
still route an `expired` resolution. Clearing the timer removes that path.
